methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective prognostic model development: 714 patients training cohort, 180 validation cohort (8:2 random split). Univariate/multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression with 22 variables. Independent prognostic factors identified: ECOG PS, pleural/peritoneal metastases, Lauren type, CRP, elevated LDH. Time-dependent ROC curves (AUC 0.71-0.78), calibration plots with 1000 bootstrap resamples, decision curve analysis. Sensitivity analysis excluding missing data documented. K-M survival analyses with HR and 95% CIs.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual cohort study (LoE: 2b) developing/validating prognostic nomogram for HER2-negative mGC on first-line PD-1 blockade (new standard of care). Addresses clinical need: patient heterogeneity in survival outcomes (mOS <18 months) requires risk stratification for personalized management. Nomogram superior to PD-L1 CPS and prior models (mGPS, RMH score, JCOG index) in discrimination.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive reporting: baseline characteristics balanced between cohorts (Table 1); univariate/multivariate Cox models with HR/95% CIs (Table 2); nomogram graphical presentation (Figure 2); risk stratification with KM curves (Figure 3). Ethics approval documented (Sun Yat-sen University, IRB 2025-015-01). Limitations acknowledged (external validation needed). Dynamic nomogram website referenced but link redacted. Supplementary materials extensive.

novelty_literature.justification: Develops first nomogram specific for HER2-negative mGC on first-line PD-1 blockade. Prior work developed model for dMMR/MSI-high mGC but not HER2-negative subset on PD-1. Integrates known prognostic factors (inflammatory markers CRP/LDH, ECOG PS, metastatic burden) into practical tool. Meaningful but incremental contribution; uses standard Cox regression, not novel statistical methods.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-structured manuscript: clear problem statement, comprehensive baseline characteristics, univariate/multivariate results systematically presented with forest plots, nomogram development explicit (5 factors selected), validation rigorous with time-dependent ROC and calibration plots. Risk stratification clinically intuitive (low/intermediate/high). Discussion contextualizes vs prior models. Minor: dense tables but necessary.

key_strengths: Large real-world cohort (n=894): 714 training, 180 validation; balanced baseline characteristics support generalizability to HER2-negative mGC on first-line PD-1 blockade
Rigorous statistical validation: time-dependent ROC (AUC 0.71-0.78), calibration plots with 1000 bootstrap resamples, decision curve analysis showing superiority vs prior models (mGPS, RMH, JCOG)

Clinically actionable: nomogram integrates 5 independent factors (ECOG PS, pleural/peritoneal metastases, Lauren type, CRP, elevated LDH) into practical risk stratification system (low/intermediate/high) enabling personalized prognostication
Appropriate comparisons: demonstrates nomogram superior discrimination vs PD-L1 CPS and multiple established prognostic indices
key_concerns: Retrospective design with inherent selection bias: single-center study (Sun Yat-sen) limits generalizability; requires external validation in independent multicenter cohort
Missing data patterns not fully characterized: >50% missingness exclusion criteria applied but specific missing rates for included variables not reported; potential bias from systematic missingness

Limited mechanistic insight: prognostic model identifies associations but does not explain biological mechanisms driving worse outcomes in high-risk patients; factors are largely inflammatory/clinical rather than molecular

Internal validation only: uses random split (8:2) but no external validation in independent cohort; author-acknowledged limitation ('external validation is needed') undermines current tier 2 recommendation
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 2 paper: rigorous prognostic model development with strong internal validation demonstrating clinical utility for risk stratification in HER2-negative mGC on first-line PD-1 blockade. Recommend minor revisions regarding external validation pathway and missing data characterization before acceptance at Tier 2.
